prompt: Complete WordFileWriter so writeWords stores a list of words one per line in a file and readWords loads them back, so a write followed by a read returns an equal list.
explanation: Files.write(path, iterable) writes each element of the collection as one line, terminating each with the platform line separator, and truncates any previous content by default -- exactly the one-word-per-line format required. Files.readAllLines performs the inverse, splitting the file on line terminators (and discarding them) into a List<String>, so the two calls round-trip any list of words, including the empty list. Both methods simply declare throws IOException so callers decide how to handle failures.
hints: java.nio.file.Files has a write overload that takes a Path and an Iterable of lines -- it writes one element per line and overwrites the old content.
Files.readAllLines(path) is the mirror image: it returns the file's lines as a List<String> without the newline characters.
If you write manually instead, remember a newline after each word, and make sure an empty list produces an empty file so the round trip still holds.
